<!--
Explain what this step does and why, and copy each command you ran into a
bash chunk. R chunks run from the top of the repository.

Answer: This step assesses the quality of the bins using checkM, checking for completeness and conteminations. Errors may occur through assembling, such as failing to join contigs from the same genome, or assembling a contig from a different genome resulting in variations in completeness or conteminations wintin thoes bins. 
-->

Completeness and contamination of each bin, estimated with CheckM, and selection of the most complete bins for further analysis. Commands for this step were run in `checkm/`.

Change working directory: 
```bash
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/checkm
```
Display lengths of all contigs (shortest to longest):
```bash
cat ../flye/bbd/assembly.fasta | bioawk -c fastx '{print length($seq),$name}' | sort -n
```
Longest contig: contig_122

Saves longest contig as a bin:
```bash
samtools faidx ../flye/bbd/assembly.fasta contig_122 > ../metabat/bins_bbd/contig_122.fa
```
Copy all bins into bins_bbd into checkm:
```bash
cp ../metabat/bins_bbd/*.fa bins_bbd/
```
Creating slurm script for checkm run:
```bash 
#!/bin/bash
#SBATCH --time=60
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=6 --mem=40gb

echo "Starting checkm in $(pwd) at $(date)"

shopt -s expand_aliases
alias checkm='apptainer run -B /pvol/:/pvol /pvol/data/sif/checkm.sif checkm'

checkm lineage_wf bins_bbd out -t 6 -x fa -f checkm_results_bbd.txt

echo "Finished checkm in $(pwd) at $(date)"
```
Submit checkm job: 
```bash 
sbatch run_checkm_bbd.sh
```
Select bins based on checkm results; 
Change director to checkm folder:
```bash 
cd ~/bbd-metagenome/checkm
```
View checkm_results_bbd.txt in terminal;
  viewing default top 10 lines:
```bash 
head checkm_results_bbd.txt 
```
Viewing top 20 lines: 
```bash 
head -n 20 checkm_results_bbd.txt 
```
Bins with completeness greater than 15%: Extracting bin ID using awk:
```bash
cat checkm_results_bbd.txt | awk '$13>15'
```
Printjust the bin ID:
```bash
cat checkm_results_bbd.txt | awk '$13>15{print $1}'
```
Sending output (bin ID) to a file (bbd_topbins.txt):
```bash
cat checkm_results_bbd.txt | awk '$13>15{print $1}' > bbd_topbins.txt
```
